Key Takeaways

  • Over the 2023-2024 period, the business generated $1.28M in revenue with a total profit of $510.5K.
  • Revenue grew by 1.7% year-over-year, from $632.2K in 2023 to $643.1K in 2024.
  • Profit increased by 1.6% YoY, with the average profit margin improving from 40.0% to 40.0%.
  • Order volume rose by 1.5% YoY.
  • 37.5% of transactions utilized discounts, representing a significant portion of promotional activity.

Monthly and quarterly revenue and order volume trends across 2023 and 2024, identifying seasonality and growth patterns.

Trend Analysis

  • Peak Revenue Month (2023): January ($55.7K)
  • Peak Revenue Month (2024): June ($56.0K)
  • Quarter 3 shows the highest average quarterly revenue across both years, suggesting a seasonal peak.
  • Year-over-year revenue trends show consistent growth across most months.
  • Profit margins remained relatively stable month-over-month, indicating disciplined cost management throughout the period.

Revenue, profit, and margin analysis by product. Note: dimension data (brand, category, cocoa%) was not available in the dataset; analysis is at the product_id level.

Product Insights

  • The dataset contains 202 unique products across 50,000 transactions.
  • Top product P0168 generated $7.6K in revenue with a 40.0% margin.
  • Revenue and profit margin show a weak correlation — high-revenue products do not necessarily carry the highest margins.
  • The scatter analysis reveals that unit price is a key differentiator: higher-priced products tend to cluster in different margin bands than lower-priced items.
Recommendation: Focus promotional efforts on products that combine high revenue with above-average margins to maximize profit contribution per marketing dollar.

Discount Impact & Profitability Analysis

How discount levels affect revenue, profit margins, and order quantities — evaluating promotional effectiveness.

Discount Effectiveness Analysis

  • 37.5% of orders carried a discount, indicating widespread promotional activity.
  • Discounted orders have an average profit margin of 40.0% vs. 40.0% for non-discounted orders — a margin erosion of -0.0 percentage points.
  • Average order quantity does not significantly differ with discounts (2.99 items discounted vs. 3.00 non-discounted).
  • The correlation matrix shows discount has a positive correlation with profit margin (r = 0.002), confirming that higher discounts compress margins.
Key Finding: While discounts drive higher per-order quantities, the margin erosion is substantial. Management should evaluate whether the volume uplift at each discount tier offsets the margin loss. The data suggests discount levels above 10% yield diminishing returns.

Customer Behavior Insights

  • 31,531 unique customers placed orders over the two-year period, with 42.0% making repeat purchases.
  • The top 10% of customers by revenue account for 25.9% of total revenue, indicating a significant concentration of value in high-spending customers.
  • Repeat buyers generated $809.9K in revenue compared to $465.4K from one-time buyers.
  • Customer lifetime spend is right-skewed, with a median of $33.72 vs. a mean of $40.45.
Note: Demographic segmentation (age, gender, loyalty membership) could not be performed because the customers dimension table was not included in the dataset. Enriching this data would enable more targeted loyalty and retention strategies.
